reason: Runnable (python3+numpy, pairs in V are 2^(2l-1)<=8192 at l<=7, far under 12 CPU-min; statistic is structural, not wall time) but as written it does NOT discriminate the mechanism. (1) Wrong statistic: the marginal Hamming weight of proj_{V^perp} x(P1+P2) is a one-list property. NN matching against x(R-P3) needs correlation between the two keys; if the R-P3 list is uniform in the projection, d(a,b)~Binomial(n-l,1/2) for ANY a, so a weight deficit in list 1 alone gives zero NN gain. The stated mechanism ('addition is near F_2-linear modulo V') is a statement about predictability of pi(x(P1+P2)) from (x(P1),x(P2)), which the weight test never touches. Also exact equality keys x(P1+P2)=x(R-P3) are already computable, so Hamming proximity only pays if a cheap approximate (linear/low-degree) predictor of pi(z) exists from the summands; that is what must be measured. (2) No null/control arm: only an analytic Binomial reference; x-coords of curve points are not exactly uniform (Tr(x)=Tr(a2)+Tr(sqrt(b)/x) constraint), so the analytic null is slightly wrong; need an empirical null from shuffled/off-V points and a positive control. (3) KS on a discrete Binomial with ties is invalid; 200 complements x 3 n with threshold p>0.01 'for all' guarantees ~6 spurious p<0.01 hits (needs min-p/Bonferroni with permutation null). (4) 'Frobenius-adapted complement' and the curve family are undefined; for prime n there is no Frobenius-stable V, and a complement chosen to minimise weight on the same pairs is overfit (selection bias) unless split train/test. Weight under a random surjective F_2-linear quotient of a uniform variable is exactly Binomial, so random complements can only show a deficit if x(P1+P2) is non-uniform, which is the trace constraint only. (5) Scaling: n in {17,19,23} (3 points, l=5..7) is too few to claim 'persisting with n'; the toy says nothing about n=131 unless a constant-epsilon trend vs l is shown against a null that decays like sqrt(l*2^-2l). The prediction ('>=5% mean deficit') does not map to a NN exponent. Even if true, CGK certificate B*D^2<<N is not addressed: a Hamming-key filter on 2-list merge is at best constant/engineering unless epsilon is constant as n grows AND the R-P3 list shares the bias.
fix: Replace the statistic. Setup: binary curve E: y^2+xy=x^3+a2x^2+b over F_{2^n}, odd n in {13,17,19,23,29} (primes) plus composites {15,21} as controls; curves: 5 random b (Tr(b)=1 for odd n) and K_0 (b=1,a2=0/1). V = random l-dim F_2-subspace, l=floor(n/3) and also l in {4..9} at n=29; factor base F={P: x(P) in V}, enumerate points with half-trace/trace solve. For every unordered pair (P1,P2) in F (<=2^17) compute z+=x(P1+P2) and z-=x(P1-P2). Fix a surjective F_2-linear quotient pi: F->F_2^(n-l) with kernel V (random and 'Frobenius-adapted' defined as pi built from the normal-basis coordinates dropping a V-basis, stated explicitly). Primary test (near-linearity): feature vector phi(P1,P2) in F_2^(2l) = (coords of x1 in V, coords of x2 in V) (optionally + l(l-1)/2 pairwise products for degree-2). For each output bit j of pi(z), compute full Walsh-Hadamard spectrum over all 2^(2l) functionals via FWHT (numpy), record eps_max = max|bias| and the best-predictor mean Hamming distance D_hat = (n-l)(1/2 - eps_avg). Null arm A: same pairs, z replaced by a random permutation of z across pairs (1000 shuffles gives empirical max-bias distribution and p-value, handles min-p over all functionals and complements). Null arm B: x of random non-V points (pairs outside V) under the same pipeline. Positive control: composite n=18, V=subfield F_{2^6} or F_{2^9}, and a planted linear map z=pi(L(x1,x2))+noise(rate q) to verify eps_max recovers 1-2q. Secondary (keep original): weight of pi(z) vs empirical shuffled null with exact binomial/chi-square test (not KS), Bonferroni across complements, with complement chosen on a train half of pairs and evaluated on the held-out half and on a fresh (b, V). Decision rule: true if eps_max exceeds the 99.9th pct of the shuffle null AND held-out eps persists with eps_max/eps_null ratio non-decreasing in l across n=13..29 AND fresh-curve replication; false if all empirical p>0.001/#tests and eps_max within null band. Report the scaling slope of eps_max vs l (null scales ~ sqrt(l/2^(2l)); a constant eps would be flat). State explicitly that a toy pass only shows persistence over l<=9 and gives no n=131 statement; claim classification stays 'engineering' unless eps is flat in l and also present between z and the x(R-P3) side with R random. Metrics are counts/biases/Hamming distance, not time. Cost: FWHT of 2^18 x (n-l) bits x 1000 shuffles is the heaviest part (~minutes); cap shuffles at 200 for l>=8.
